ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the picture, three kinds of building blocks are given: a light gray L-shaped building block, composed of 5 small cubes; a dark gray long-strip building block, composed of 3 small cubes; and a white small cube, which is 1 unit cube. What is assembled on the right side is a 3×3×3 large cube. According to the visible color and shape arrangement on the right side, it can be counted that 2 light gray L-shaped building blocks and 2 dark gray long-strip building blocks are used, and the remaining positions are filled with white small cubes. Reasoning: The 3×3×3 large cube has 27 unit small-cube positions in total. 2 light gray L-shaped building blocks occupy 2×5=10 unit cubes, and 2 dark gray long-strip building blocks occupy 2×3=6 unit cubes, occupying 16 unit cubes in total. Therefore the number of white small cubes is 27−16=11.

raw_record.question_text: The big cube is made up of three different kinds of building blocks (see diagram). How many of the little white cubes are needed for this big cube?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the three available block types are a light-gray L-shaped block made from 5 unit cubes, a dark rectangular rod made from 3 unit cubes, and a single white unit cube. The assembled solid on the right is a 3 by 3 by 3 cube, so it contains 27 unit-cube positions in total. From the visible arrangement of the big cube, count the non-white blocks used: there are 2 light-gray L blocks and 2 dark rods. These account for 2×5 + 2×3 = 16 unit cubes. Subtract from the full cube volume: 27 − 16 = 11 little white cubes.
